html:
A Turkish dynasty's empire that ruled much of southeastern Europe, West Asia and North Africa for some six centuries. It began around 1299 as a small principality in northwest Anatolia and ended in 1922, after defeat in the First World War.

The house of Osman held the throne the whole time, an unusually long run. The state rested on a slave army and administration (the janissaries and palace officials, recruited partly from Christian boys), on Islamic and sultan's law, and on letting Christian and Jewish communities run their own affairs.

Main stages:

  • About 1299. Osman I leads one of the Turkish principalities that rose as Seljuk Anatolia broke up.
  • 1354. The Ottomans take Gallipoli and push into the Balkans. In 1402 Timur crushes Sultan Bayezid at Ankara, but the state recovers.
  • 1453. Mehmed II takes Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire. It becomes Istanbul, the capital.
  • 1516 to 1517. Selim I takes Syria and Egypt, and with them Mecca and Medina.
  • 1520 to 1566. Suleiman the Magnificent takes Hungary and lays siege to Vienna. The empire is at its peak.
  • 1683. A second siege of Vienna fails, and a long retreat in Europe begins.
  • 1839 to 1876. The Tanzimat reforms try to modernise law, army and taxes.

In the 1800s the empire lost Greece, Egypt, the Balkans and North Africa, and it borrowed heavily from European banks. It entered the First World War on Germany's side. During the war its government carried out the Armenian genocide. After defeat the Allies planned to carve up even Anatolia. A national movement fought them off, abolished the sultanate in 1922, and founded the Republic of Turkey in 1923.
sum: A Turkish dynasty's empire that ruled much of southeastern Europe, West Asia and North Africa for some six centuries. It began around 1299 as a small principality in northwest Anatolia and ended in 1922, after defeat in the First World War.
